title: Introduce chrono-range instrumentation and mini benchdriver for kernel/kv microbenchmarks
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Added a lightweight chrono-based instrumentation API and a small benchdriver to run microbenchmarks for kernel selection, KV cache priming, and continuous batching simulations. No user-facing API changes. Useful for internal perf tuning and dashboard exports.
description:
Summary: Adds a lightweight, dependency-free chrono-range instrumentation layer (chrono::Range) plus a minimal benchdriver that runs targeted microbenchmarks for kernel selection heuristics, KV cache priming behavior, and continuous-batching tradeoffs.
Motivation: Existing tracing hooks (NVTX, perfetto exporters) are heavy or platform-specific; we needed a low-overhead, portable way to add fine-grained timing and counter probes inside the hot path to drive scheduler decisions and quantized-kernel comparisons.
This PR introduces:
1) src/runtime/profiling/chrono.{h,cpp}: a tiny RAII-style range timer with optional histogram aggregator and exported labels; designed to be inlinable and safe on hot paths.
2) runtime/metrics/occupancy_counters.cpp: lightweight per-thread occupancy counters and a sampled atomic counter that can be toggled at runtime.
3) tools/microbench/benchdriver.py: benchdriver that spins synthetic workloads (varying batch sizes, kv cache hit distributions, and sequence length profiles) and drives kernel selector permutations while collecting chrono ranges and counters.
4) tools/microbench/configs/kv_priming.yaml: example workloads to reproduce KV priming regressions.
5) dashboards/perf/csv_exporter.go: a tiny exporter that converts benchdriver output into CSVs compatible with our perf dashboard ingestion.
6) tests/perf/test_kernel_selection.cc and small doc src/docs/perf/chrono-instrumentation.md showing how to run and interpret outputs.
Design notes:
- Chrono::Range avoids external dependencies and is intended for short-lived ranges; it supports labels, a sampled flag, and a histogram bucket pass-through to the existing metrics registry.
- Benchdriver runs combinations in deterministic order and supports warm-up phases to populate KV caches and primed KV hit ratios; it also simulates concurrent inference load to exercise batching windows.
- Exporter produces per-range latency p50/p95/p99 and occupancy counts per sample to enable cross-correlation in the perf dashboard.
Performance: Benchmarks run in CI microbench target showed <1.8% overhead at default sampling, and <0.2% when sampling is disabled. Typical bench runs produce expected trends: some kernel variants favor shorter sequences with lower occupancy; KV priming reduces median latency by ~12% in synthetic priming scenario.
Backwards compatibility & safety: No breaking API changes. Chrono instrumentation is opt-in via a runtime flag (RUNTIME_CHRONO=1) and default sampling is on for internal builds only.
CI and tests: Added unit tests for the chrono histogram aggregator and a small integration test that validates benchdriver CSV output schema.
Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Benchdriver smoke runs
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] Metrics export compatibility validated
How to run locally: python tools/microbench/benchdriver.py --config tools/microbench/configs/kv_priming.yaml --export csv --out /tmp/bench.csv; then run tools/perf/ingest-dashboard --source /tmp/bench.csv for local inspection in dev dashboard.

Review conversation: Tomás Rivera (2024-11-16): Great direction, can we avoid any heap allocations in the hot path? Suggest inline buckets and stack-only buffers.
Aisha Kapoor (2024-11-16): Agreed. Updated chrono.h to keep buckets on the caller stack and use a pointer to registry when enabled. No allocations on the common path.

Ethan Liu (2024-11-17): CI failed on linux-integration (timeout) during benchdriver run; looks like the smoke config had an infinite loop on rare seeds. Please add a hard timeout and deterministic RNG seed.
Aisha Kapoor (2024-11-17): Added timeout param and fixed RNG seed handling; re-ran CI.
Priya Menon (2024-11-18): Please document the sampling knobs and ensure default is off for public builds. Also request a brief note linking to ENG-7192 for team visibility.
Aisha Kapoor (2024-11-18): Docs updated; sampling default set to off in OSS builds, internal builds keep sampling on. Linked the linear issue in the description.

CI Bot (2024-11-19): Rerun CI: all checks passed.
Tomás Rivera (2024-11-20): Approve after addressing allocation and timeout comments.
Testing & CI notes: Initial CI job timed out due to benchdriver long run; added timeout flag and adjusted CI profile to use smaller synthetic workloads for integration. All tests green on rerun.
Additional context: This PR is intended to be a minimal, portable instrumentation layer that complements existing heavy-weight tracers (NVTX, perfetto) and is optimized for microbench-driven kernel/scheduler tuning. Followups planned: auto-correlation exporter to link KV cache hit traces to kernel selection decisions, and a lightweight web UI to visualize benchdriver runs. See ENG-7341 for follow-up tasks.
